questions.q: Why does an inbound Scripted REST API resource typically need to call JSON.parse() on the request body before using its data?
options: Because the request body arrives as a raw string, and parsing converts it into a usable object with real properties
Because GlideRecord requires all input to be pre-encrypted
Because JSON.parse() validates the caller's authentication
Because the request body is always already an object and parsing is optional
questions.explain: The raw body text has no usable properties until it's parsed into an actual JavaScript object.

questions.q: What is true about JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(x)) for a plain object x?
options: It always throws an error
It returns an object equivalent to the original x — the two operations are inverses
It returns the string representation of x, not an object
It deletes all numeric properties from x
questions.explain: Stringifying and then parsing is a round-trip: the result is an equivalent object to the one you started with.
